paper_metadata.title: Dendrite growth and defects formation with increasing withdrawal rates in the rejoined platforms of Ni-based single crystal superalloys

evidence.quote: The effect of withdrawal rates on the dendrite growth and defects formation in the rejoined platforms of a Ni-based single crystal superalloy during directi onal solidification was studied by experimental investigations and ProCAST simulations.
Content of alloy elements in the different regions of the rejoined platforms at the withdrawal rates of 150 µm/s after solidification.

mechanisms.name: orientation deviation under unstable thermal field

evidence.quote: It meant that the orientation of these long secondary dendrites with lateral growth would deviate during their growth process in the unstable thermal field.
A Ni-based superalloy with composition of 5.6 Al, 7 .5 Ta, 2.0 Mo, 8.0 W, 2.0 Re, 4.3 Cr, 9.0 Co, 0.5 Nb, 0.1 Hf, 0.006 C, and the balance Ni(mass fracti on) was used in current experiments.
Firstly, the furnace chamber was vacuumed and the mold shell was preheated to 1540 ºC. Secondly, the superheated molten alloy (1580 °C) was poured into the mould and held for 10 min.
Finally, the ceramic mold was pulled out from the f urnace at predetermined withdrawal rates: 60 µm/s, 75 µm/s, 100 µm/s and 150 µm/s.
Region I, the original primary dendrite arm s grew regularly and were cross-shaped with four orthogonal secondary dendrite arms
Region II, it was mainly composed of long secondary dendrite arms which were formed through lateral growth.
Meanwhile, a GB was pr oduced when the dendrites converged in the middle region of the platforms, as shown in Fig. 3c .
Their corresponding polar diagrams in Figs. 4c and 4d showed that they were LABs.
some broken ternary b ranches at the root of the long secondary branches appeared near the crisscross position in the region M of the platform
a new region with a la rge number of small detached ternary arms were observed in the region M, as shown the region III in Fig. 5a
almost all th e ternary dendrite arms detached from their parent arms. The integrity of the single crystal was compl etely destroyed.
Therefore, it indicated that the lateral gro wth of secondary branches in the platforms was inevitable and was more severe at higher withdrawal rates.
if these long secondary branches were regarded as some cantilever beams, they were easy t o deform under the thermal contraction stresses and led to orientation deviation
Finally, these secon dary dendrites with different orientations produced some LABs once they converged, as shown the LABs-I and LABs-II in Fig. 4a.
Consequently, a remelting process at the roots was initiated driven by solute enrichment.
Consequently, s ome of fragile ternary branches around the primary stems were subjected to enrichment of solute in poc kets and remelted from their parent stems.
Finally, the solute enrichment in the region III was severe enough to cause the decre ase of solidus temperature [31], and most of ternar y arms in the region III remelted from their parent a rms.
Furthermore, the unstable th ermal field in the region M could also lead to solu te enrichment.

With the withdrawal rate was increased to 150 µm/s, a new region with a large area of fragments formed in the middle regions of the platforms, whic h was caused by the solute enrichment leading to the reduction of solidus.

Once the withdrawal rate exceeded 100 µm/s, the local ternary dendrite fragments appeared in the middle regions of the platforms, which were caused by the solute enrichment at the fragile ternary dendrite roots in the pockets around the primary stems.
